title: Zipf's Law: Why Does the Same Pattern Show Up in Words, Cities, and Earthquakes?
question: Why do wildly unrelated things—word frequencies, city populations, company sizes, even earthquake magnitudes—all follow the same simple mathematical curve?
summary: An eerie statistical regularity, first noticed in word frequencies, keeps reappearing across nature and society, suggesting a shared logic behind how rank and size relate in systems that grow over time.
